notes: MONEY BANKED NOW REACHES THE RECONCILIATION FROM EVERY SCREEN. The lodgement register was filled by Fund Receipts and by nothing else, while the reconciliation screen said in as many words that it fills itself. Money banked in settlement of an invoice recorded nothing, and neither did the proceeds of an asset sold, cash returned when a petty-cash float is closed, or the receiving side of a transfer between your own accounts. Every one of those now enters the register, so the month they were banked no longer reconciles short by their value with nothing on the page to explain it. A CORRECTED CHEQUE NO LONGER REWRITES HISTORY. Keeping the same cheque number on a correction — which the app itself tells you to do — used to rewrite the date the reconciliation reads. A cheque written in January, corrected in March, stopped ever having been outstanding in January, so reprinting that already-signed-off month came back short by its value. A cheque the bank has ALREADY PAID now keeps the date and the amount it was actually paid for, because those are facts about the bank that re-coding our own entry does not change. One still outstanding keeps a record of the month it was outstanding in. Either way, a month you have signed off reprints as you signed it off. CORRECTING A RECEIPT NO LONGER BREAKS THE RECONCILIATION. Correcting a receipt the bank had already credited left a second lodgement for the same deposit that could never be cleared — the bank's own credit line had been used by the first — so every reconciliation from then on carried an uncredited lodgement that did not exist, and the month could not be signed off at all. WITHHOLDING TAX. Correcting a payment that paid several people no longer re-works each person's deduction from TODAY's rates: what was actually withheld is carried through. A withholding certificate and a GRA schedule now print the rate that was ACTUALLY deducted, so reprinting an earlier month after a rate change no longer certifies a 7.5% deduction at 5% — the office copy and the supplier's copy agree again. Recording a missing cheque against an already-posted remittance refuses a blank number instead of reporting success and writing nothing. BUDGETS AND REVERSALS. A commitment entered with an earlier date now reserves the budget of ITS OWN year rather than the current one. The Approval Centre's reversal tool reads the whole ledger instead of only the newest 300 vouchers — it is the only route back for a payroll or a remittance voucher, and an older one had become impossible to reach. BACKUPS. A backup's checksum is now written into place before the archive it protects. Version .62 announced that change; it had been described but never actually made, and the gap stayed open another week. It is real now, and proved by a test. The off-site copy also chose which old backups to delete by the file's date on disk rather than the date in its name — so a cloud folder that re-dated files could delete the newest ledger and keep the oldest. And deleting a company whose books were not on this computer used to create an empty database in their place, which silenced the warning that the books were missing and sent nobody looking for the copy that still existed. ALSO IN THIS VERSION, though it will not appear for a school or an NGO: an organisation that is registered for VAT and sells over a counter can now tick "VAT-able sale" on a receipt and have the VAT inside the money received reach the VAT return. The option is offered only where an administrator has said the organisation is VAT-registered and named the account, so fund receipts that are not VAT-able supplies never see it. HOW THIS RELEASE WAS CHECKED. Thirty independent reviewers went over everything added in the last two releases; twenty-three findings were confirmed and all twenty-three are fixed. Five of the automated guards that are supposed to stop such defects returning turned out not to work — each could be made to pass over the very bug it was written for — and every one has been repaired and then deliberately broken to prove it now fails. A new test drives the installed application through a month of ordinary work and reads the ledger's own totals back off the screen to check that the books balance.
